pains.title: Package, membership and gift card cash that looks like profit
pains.problem: Med spas get paid before the treatment happens. Booked as revenue on the day of payment, prepaid packages and gift cards make profit look better than it is.
pains.how: Lucid sets up a prepaid and membership liability account, reconciles point of sale sales to deposits with a monthly rollforward, and reports earned revenue next to cash collected. Your CPA keeps tax timing separate.

pains.title: Laser and device purchases that are hard to judge
pains.problem: One energy device can cost a six figure amount. The real question is how many paid treatments cover the payment, consumables and service plan.
pains.how: Before you buy, Lucid builds a payback model from your quote and financing terms. Afterward it reports profit by service. Lucid does not arrange financing.

pains.title: Injectables, product cost and provider profit across locations
pains.problem: Neurotoxin and filler are costly and perishable. Expensed on purchase, one big order spikes a month and hides the margin on each treatment.
pains.how: Lucid reports product cost by service line. Each location gets its own books on one chart of accounts, plus a combined view. Your CPA reviews W-2 versus 1099 injector pay.

faq_title: Med spa accounting questions owners ask
cta: Book a free 30 minute consult. Bring your point of sale reports and latest P&L, and Lucid will show you what your memberships and packages really earn. Terms are month to month.

faq.q: What is the best bookkeeping service for a med spa with multiple locations?
faq.a: Look for a team that gives each location its own books, a combined view, membership and package revenue recognition, injectable cost by service and a dedicated CPA. Lucid gives you all of that, publishes its pricing and works month to month.

faq.q: Do I count med spa package and membership sales as revenue when the client pays?
faq.a: Usually not in your books. Money paid for treatments you have not delivered yet is a liability until the client uses them. Lucid tracks that balance each month so your profit reflects what you earned, and your CPA handles how it is treated for taxes separately.

faq.q: Should I buy or lease a laser for my med spa, and can I write it off?
faq.a: It depends on how many paid treatments you can do each month, the consumable cost per treatment and your tax situation. A purchased device may qualify for a first year deduction, but a deduction does not make a device pay for itself. Lucid builds a payback and tax plan from your quote before you sign.

faq.q: How do I track Botox and filler cost in my med spa books?
faq.a: Injectables are normally booked as an asset on the balance sheet and moved to cost of goods as they are used. That way one large order does not distort profit and you can see your margin on each treatment. Lucid reports product cost by service line.

faq.q: How do I keep the books for my med spa management company and the medical practice?
faq.a: Each entity needs its own books, with the management fee recorded the same way on both sides. Mixing the two makes reports unreliable. Lucid keeps them separate and gives you a combined view. Your healthcare attorney confirms the structure.
